# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👍 👍 👍 👌 👍 👎 👍 👍 👌 👍 👍 👎 👌 👍 ✊ 👍 👎 👍 👌 👍 👌 👎 👍 👍 ✊ 👎 👎 👍 👌 👍 👎 👍 👌 👍 👌 👍 👌 👎 👍 ✊ 👎 👍 👎 👎 👌 👍 👌 👍 👎 👍 👍 👌 👍 👎 👍 👍 👌 👎 👎 👎 ✊ 👎 👍 👎 👎 👌 👍 👌 👍 👎 👍 👍 👌 👍 👎 👍 👍 👌 👎 👎 👎 ✊ 👎 👎 👍 👌 👍 👎 👍 👌 👍 👌 👍 👌 👎 👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

I can see the bomb’s current state: the display reads 0, the light is blue, and the three wires are green, yellow, and red in positions 1, 2, and 3. I am telling both teammates so the Mute can apply the manual and the Blind can identify the physical controls and wires.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Bomb view: display 0. Light blue. Wire 1 green, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 red.")
speak(to="blind", text="Bomb view: display 0. Light blue. Wire 1 green, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 red.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]

The bomb remains unchanged: display 0, blue light, and wires green-yellow-red. The Mute has now signalled 🤟, but no shared meaning for that sign has been established, so I should not interpret it as an instruction. I will report it to the Blind and reiterate the visible state.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="The Mute signalled 🤟. I do not know its meaning. Bomb still shows display 0, blue light, wire 1 green, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 red.")
```

The long gesture stream from the Mute is not safely decodable from the available established meanings; I should not infer an operation from it. The bomb still visibly shows display 0, blue light, and wires green, yellow, red. I am asking the Mute to give the Blind the manual’s instruction directly by speech, while informing the Blind of the unchanged bomb state.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="The Mute sent a long gesture code whose meaning is not established. Bomb remains display 0, blue light, wire 1 green, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 red. Ask the Mute to state the manual instruction aloud.")
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot safely decode the long gesture stream. Please state the manual instruction aloud directly to the Blind, including the required operation and any wire or display conditions.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👍 👍 👍 👌 👍 👎 👍 👌 👍 👎 👎 👌 👍 👎 👍 👌 👍 👌 👎 👍 👍 👌 👎 👎 👎 👌 👍 👍 👍 👎 👎]

The Mute’s latest stream still has no agreed code, so treating it as Morse or binary could cause a fatal mistake. I will establish a precise encoding that the Mute can follow: thumbs-up as dot, thumbs-down as dash, OK as a letter separator, and fist as a word separator. The Blind will also know the mapping and can act once I relay the decoded manual instruction.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please resend the manual instruction using this exact Morse code: 👍 means dot, 👎 means dash, 👌 separates letters, ✊ separates words. Send only the encoded instruction.")
speak(to="blind", text="The Mute will resend the manual instruction in Morse. Decode with thumbs-up as dot, thumbs-down as dash, OK as letter separator, and fist as word separator. I will relay the decoded text.")
```

Using the encoding I specified, the beginning decodes clearly as “DISPLAY 0 BLUE,” but the next groups decode to nonsensical text (“NENE MIRE…”), so I cannot safely infer the required operation or wire. The bomb remains unchanged. I am asking the Mute to resend more slowly with explicit separators and asking the Blind not to act on this ambiguous message.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I decode the start as DISPLAY 0 BLUE, but the remainder is ambiguous or malformed. Please resend the complete instruction slowly, using ✊ between words and 👌 between every letter, with no extra gestures.")
speak(to="blind", text="The code clearly says DISPLAY 0 BLUE, but the remainder is ambiguous and does not identify a safe operation. Do not act yet; I have asked the Mute to resend it with explicit separators.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👍 👍 👌 👍 👍 👌 👍 👍 👍 👌 👍 👎 👎 👍 👌 👍 👎 👍 👍 👌 👍 👎 👌 👎 👍 👎 👎 ✊ 👎 👎 👎 👎 👎 ✊ 👎 👍 👍 👍 👌 👍 👎 👍 👍 👌 👍 👎 👌 👍 👍 👎 👌 👍 ✊ 👎 👍 👎 👍 👌 👍 👍 👎 👌 👎 ✊ 👍 👎 👎 👌 👍 👍 👌 👎 👍 👌 👍 ✊ 👍 👍 👍 👌 👎 👎]

The established Morse decoding now gives `DISPLAY 0 BLUE CUT WINE`, followed by an incomplete/invalid final group. This does not safely identify a wire; “WINE” is likely a transmission or encoding error, so the Blind must not cut anything yet. I am relaying the exact partial decode and asking the Mute to correct only the ambiguous portion.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Decoded instruction so far: DISPLAY 0 BLUE CUT WINE. The final code is incomplete, and WINE does not identify a wire. Do not cut anything yet.")
speak(to="mute", text="I decode DISPLAY 0 BLUE CUT WINE, then an incomplete group. Please resend only the operation and wire number, using Morse: 👍 dot, 👎 dash, 👌 letter separator, ✊ word separator.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👍 👎 👍 👌 👍 👍 👎 👌 👎 ✊ 👍 👎 👎 👌 👍 👍 👌 👍 👎 👍 👌 👍 ✊ 👍 👍 👍 👎 👎]

The Morse decodes exactly as `CUT WIRE 3`, with the final group being the Morse digit 3 (`...--`), not the letter E. This is now a clear instruction: cut wire 3, which I can identify visually as the red wire. I am telling the Blind to cut the red wire in position 3.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Confirmed instruction: CUT WIRE 3. Wire 3 is the red wire. Cut the red wire.")
speak(to="mute", text="The instruction decoded clearly as CUT WIRE 3; wire 3 is red.")
```
